lines.watchItem: Advanced packaging stays sold out with 52-78 week lead times even as monthly CoWoS capacity climbs toward 125,000-130,000 wafers, and the supply-demand gap is only expected to narrow from about 20% to about 10% by end-2026. Whether that gap closes or reopens sets how much of the booked accelerator demand can actually ship.

Packaging output is heavily tied to three buyers, with one at about 60% and another at about 11%, and that second buyer is splitting its slice between server CPUs and its new accelerators. Any swing in one customer's ordering moves a large share of packaging loading.

High-bandwidth memory is sold out through 2026 with much of 2027 pre-booked, contract prices are forecast to roughly double into 2027, and one supplier says it cannot see when supply catches up. Memory scarcity can cap accelerator shipments even when packaging and wafer capacity are available.

Demand momentum is very strong across the value chain: record data-center revenue up 92% year over year, hyperscaler 2026 capex guided near $660-725 billion, and cloud backlog rising past $500 billion. Wafer-start planning at the leading edge sits directly under that pull, with the caveat that memory and packaging gate what converts to shipments.

Custom accelerators are growing far faster than merchant GPUs — forecast 44.6% versus 16.1% for 2026, with custom silicon already reported at roughly two-thirds of AI compute and new in-house parts entering production this September. The leading-node customer base is shifting from a few merchant-GPU vendors toward hyperscaler programs, most of which run through two design houses.

The second merchant vendor is converting gigawatt-scale commitments — Meta, OpenAI, Oracle, Microsoft and now a 2 GW Anthropic deal — into data-center revenue up 57% year over year, but its rack-scale ramp slips to Q2 2027 and its share is still only about 5-7%. How fast those commitments turn into volume changes the mix of leading-node customers.

Pricing along the chain stays firm: 75% non-GAAP gross margin at the lead vendor, 67.7% foundry gross margin with 2026 revenue growth guided above 40%, rental prices up 24% off their late-2025 low, and rack component costs inflating 2-3% per week on memory scarcity. Firm end pricing and scarce capacity are what keep sellers in the stronger bargaining position.

Policy and competitive moves cut both ways: China licensing moved to case-by-case review with a cap under half of comparable US sales while actual shipments stay trivial and one vendor's China revenue halved, a smuggling probe is widening, a rival foundry added Intel 3 capacity in Ireland and signed a named external customer, and Chinese labs trained a frontier model on 50,000 domestic accelerators. Each is a path by which foundry demand could shift.
